newsitem.title: USA: Prodi denies pressing central bank for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Prodi denies pressing central bank for rate cut.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday he had never tried to put pressure on the Bank of Italy's Governor to cut the discount rate.

"I have never harassed anyone" Prodi told a news conference when asked whether he was aware of a plea by Fiat's honorary President Gianni Agnelli to leave the central bank to decide a cut in its own time.

Asked whether he did not think it was time for a discount rate cut, Prodi said that "discount rate cuts are decided by the Bank of Italy governor... It's on the basis of stable low inflation that a cut is decided."
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio has kept the discount rate firmly pegged at 6.75 percent since January despite a steady fall in the headline rate of inflation.
Fazio's caution has drawn criticism from economists who believe an opportunity to lower borrowing costs is being missed.
Prodi said a discount rate cut was possible "in the foreseeable future, when the fight against inflation is won."
"Inflation may rise by a tenth of a point or so, but I don't believe there are any elements that point to a new rise in inflation" Prodi said .

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Saturday that inflation will remain in the 1.5 to 1.8/1.9 pct range this year. Preliminary data released by a sample of Italian cities on Friday showed year-on-year inflation running at 1.5 percent in June.
